messages.text: What evidence is required to compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for Wireless Communication without making unsupported claims?

**Our official R&S specifications and feature documents for each product being claimed.** For CMX500, the binding specifications are in `CMX500_specs_en_5216-4127-22_v1100`, while `CMX500_Features_CSW9-20-0_en_32` is a features/functions overview and states that data without tolerance limits is not binding [25].
For CMX500 product claims, cite the specs/features that state it is a one-box network emulation and measurement solution supporting LTE, NR FR1, NR FR2, NSA, SA, FDD and TDD, plus supported signaling/application/measurement features such as WLAN, fading, AWGN, BLER, throughput and IP traffic analysis [22][23].
**Exact R&S option codes and orderable configurations for signaling claims.** CMX500 signaling comparisons need option-code evidence for NR, LTE, WLAN, RedCap, eRedCap, NTN and NB-NTN capabilities, such as CMX-KS600B/M/X for NR signaling Rel. 15, CMX-KS500B/M/X for LTE signaling, CMX-KS350B–KS357B for WLAN signaling, CMX-KS617B/M/X for RedCap, CMX-KS618B/X for eRedCap, and CMX-KS627B/M/X, KS628B/X, KS629B/X for NTN [24][26][55][58][60].
**Official R&S specifications for non-signaling tester claims.** CMP200 claims need the CMP200 specifications, which state that CMP200 with CMPHEAD30/CMPHEAD50 forms a 5G NR FR2 mmWave nonsignaling one-box test solution for R&D RF parametric testing, manufacturing high-volume RF parametric testing, and mmWave radiated/conducted setups [31][33].
CMP180 claims need CMP180 documentation showing it is a Radio Communication Tester for production / wireless communication device testing, with simultaneous receiver/transmitter testing and multi-port RF generator/analyzer architecture [36][37][38].
**Product-data conditions, calibration and binding-status evidence.** CMX500 specifications apply only under stated conditions including warm-up, environmental conditions, recommended calibration interval and internal adjustments, and non-traceable/typical/nominal/measured values are not guaranteed [25].
CMP200 specifications likewise distinguish guaranteed specifications from non-traceable, typical, nominal and measured values, and list recommended calibration intervals [30][35].
CMP180 documentation lists calibration interval and warranty information [39].
**Competitor official datasheets, brochures, configuration guides or third-party evidence for every competitor capability or limitation.** The Anritsu comparison page states that R&S battle-card claims should not be used in customer documents without Anritsu official data and third-party evidence [10].
The Keysight battle card notes that its claims about Keysight portfolio, architecture, software, support, Wi‑Fi, RedCap and FR3/6G lack Keysight official datasheets or versioned documentation [63].
The amarisoft comparison table states that multiple claims lack third-party or amarisoft official documentation and that production-platform specifications must be cited separately [3].
**Conformance / certification evidence when claiming operator acceptance, PTCRB, GCF or pre-conformance advantages.** The amarisoft battle card says needs should be separated by whether PTCRB/GCF-aligned test cases, operator acceptance, conformance or pre-conformance are required, but also notes that test package option codes or accreditation documents are not listed [2][3].
Internal RF/RRM and GCF/PTCRB updates are not official GCF/PTCRB/CTIA minutes or validation reports and lack complete datasets, test case IDs, band combinations or methodology [49][50].
**Comparable test conditions and configuration evidence for performance claims.** Claims about FR1/FR2/FR3 bandwidth, data rate, fading, IP throughput, Wi‑Fi integration or “one-box” capability need formal datasheets, option-code mapping, throughput profiles and test conditions, because the Anritsu comparison flags missing official datasheets, option-code cross-references and test conditions for several such claims [6].
The Keysight battle card similarly says “only platform,” “industry-leading,” “fully integrated,” “long-term scalability” and “lower TCO” are sales language and require formal datasheets, features documents, conformance reports or configuration tools before being treated as verifiable claims [61].
**No use of internal battle-card language as verified competitor fact unless independently supported.** Anritsu “fragmented tools” positioning can remain R&S sales positioning, but Anritsu’s own brochure supports that MX844030PC uses a common RTD GUI for protocol test case transfer, so the internal characterization cannot be treated as Anritsu official specification [9].
Internal O-RU competitor, price-point, market-share and test-coverage comparisons require official competitor datasheets, solution briefs, market reports, quotes, contracts or release notes before use as verified claims [14][18][21][43].
**Evidence for cost, TCO, support, warranty and calibration claims.** Sales statements such as fewer calibrations, fewer licenses, lower TCO and higher throughput are not supported by a TCO calculation in the cited battle card [8].
Competitor support or warranty claims require official service terms, since KeysightCare claims lack cited service-term documents and Anritsu support claims lack Anritsu official or third-party sources [13][63].
【推論】A defensible comparison package should therefore pair R&S CMX500/CMP180/CMP200 official specifications, feature documents, option codes, calibration conditions and conformance evidence with the competitor’s official datasheets/configuration/service/conformance evidence for the same test scope, and avoid “only,” “best,” “lower TCO,” “accepted,” or competitor-limitation claims unless those exact claims are supported by such evidence [10][25][35][49][50][61][63].

passages.text:
R&S CMX500 vs amarisoft › 核心 thesis
依 [[2026_02_CMX500_Amarisoft_Sales_Battle_Card]]（2026-02-26），R&S 對 [[amarisoft]] 的核心定位是：[[R&S CMX500]] 與 R&S radio communication tester portfolio 提供 instrument-grade、validated、calibrated、可延伸至 production 的 5G testing path；[[amarisoft]] 則被描述為 COTS hardware + software-defined stack 的 functional testing solution。

R&S CMX500 vs amarisoft › Sales landmines
[[2026_02_CMX500_Amarisoft_Sales_Battle_Card]] 建議用以下問題區分需求：

1. 是否需要 calibrated [[FR2]] / [[mmWave]] testing？
2. 是否需要 global support、multi-year warranty 或 calibration services？
3. 是否需要 [[Operator Acceptance]]、[[Conformance Testing]] 或 pre-conformance？
4. 是否需要 validated / [[PTCRB]] / [[GCF]] aligned test cases，而不只是 functional simulation？
5. 是否需要 non-signaling ATE 或 multi-port production test？
6. 是否需要 integrated [[Wi-Fi signaling]]（6/6E/7）？
7. 是否需要 factory line 的 non-signaling test capability？
8. 是否需要 3GPP RF pre-conformance 或 aligned test coverage？

R&S CMX500 vs amarisoft › 對比表
| 主題 | R&S / CMX500 positioning | amarisoft positioning | 來源限制 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 公司與支援 | Global support、field engineering、calibration labs、service contracts、multi-year warranties | small French private company；remote-only support；no global footprint | [[2026_02_CMX500_Amarisoft_Sales_Battle_Card]] 未引用第三方或 amarisoft 官方文件 |
| FR1 / FR2 | [[R&S CMX500]] covers FR1、FR2 up to 50 GHz / calibrated FR2 | external RRH for FR2，calibration 以問號標示 | “up to 50 GHz” 為 battle card 說法；正式規格需引用 [[CMX500_specs_en_5216-4127-22_v1100]] |
| Wi-Fi signaling | [[R&S CMX500]] integrated Wi-Fi signaling，含 Wi-Fi 6/6E/7 | external AP/N3IWF 或 no Wi-Fi signaling | Wi-Fi feature 需回查 [[CMX500_Features_CSW9-20-0_en_32]] |
| Conformance / operator acceptance | PTCRB/GCF aligned RF、RRM、protocol、IMS、VoNR、throughput、CA、mobility tests | functional only；not accepted for operator certification | 來源未列 test package option code 或 accreditation 文件 |
| Validated NTN | validated NR-NTN RF / RRM / protocol testcases，來源括註 w/ Samsung | functional simulation only | 未列 Samsung validation report 或 test case list |
| Legacy RAT | [[R&S CMW500]] 支援 2G/3G continuity | no 2G/3G stack | CMW500 正式能力需引用 [[CMW_dat-sw_en_5213-9211-22_v1700]] |

**Our official R&S specifications and feature documents for each product being claimed.** For CMX500, the binding specifications are in `CMX500_specs_en_5216-4127-22_v1100`, while `CMX500_Features_CSW9-20-0_en_32` is a features/functions overview and states that data without tolerance limits is not binding [25].
For CMX500 product claims, cite the specs/features that state it is a one-box network emulation and measurement solution supporting LTE, NR FR1, NR FR2, NSA, SA, FDD and TDD, plus supported signaling/application/measurement features such as WLAN, fading, AWGN, BLER, throughput and IP traffic analysis [22][23].
**Exact R&S option codes and orderable configurations for signaling claims.** CMX500 signaling comparisons need option-code evidence for NR, LTE, WLAN, RedCap, eRedCap, NTN and NB-NTN capabilities, such as CMX-KS600B/M/X for NR signaling Rel. 15, CMX-KS500B/M/X for LTE signaling, CMX-KS350B–KS357B for WLAN signaling, CMX-KS617B/M/X for RedCap, CMX-KS618B/X for eRedCap, and CMX-KS627B/M/X, KS628B/X, KS629B/X for NTN [24][26][55][58][60].
**Official R&S specifications for non-signaling tester claims.** CMP200 claims need the CMP200 specifications, which state that CMP200 with CMPHEAD30/CMPHEAD50 forms a 5G NR FR2 mmWave nonsignaling one-box test solution for R&D RF parametric testing, manufacturing high-volume RF parametric testing, and mmWave radiated/conducted setups [31][33].
CMP180 claims need CMP180 documentation showing it is a Radio Communication Tester for production / wireless communication device testing, with simultaneous receiver/transmitter testing and multi-port RF generator/analyzer architecture [36][37][38].
**Product-data conditions, calibration and binding-status evidence.** CMX500 specifications apply only under stated conditions including warm-up, environmental conditions, recommended calibration interval and internal adjustments, and non-traceable/typical/nominal/measured values are not guaranteed [25].
CMP200 specifications likewise distinguish guaranteed specifications from non-traceable, typical, nominal and measured values, and list recommended calibration intervals [30][35].
CMP180 documentation lists calibration interval and warranty information [39].
**Competitor official datasheets, brochures, configuration guides or third-party evidence for every competitor capability or limitation.** The Anritsu comparison page states that R&S battle-card claims should not be used in customer documents without Anritsu official data and third-party evidence [10].
The Keysight battle card notes that its claims about Keysight portfolio, architecture, software, support, Wi‑Fi, RedCap and FR3/6G lack Keysight official datasheets or versioned documentation [63].
The amarisoft comparison table states that multiple claims lack third-party or amarisoft official documentation and that production-platform specifications must be cited separately [3].
**Conformance / certification evidence when claiming operator acceptance, PTCRB, GCF or pre-conformance advantages.** The amarisoft battle card says needs should be separated by whether PTCRB/GCF-aligned test cases, operator acceptance, conformance or pre-conformance are required, but also notes that test package option codes or accreditation documents are not listed [2][3].
Internal RF/RRM and GCF/PTCRB updates are not official GCF/PTCRB/CTIA minutes or validation reports and lack complete datasets, test case IDs, band combinations or methodology [49][50].
**Comparable test conditions and configuration evidence for performance claims.** Claims about FR1/FR2/FR3 bandwidth, data rate, fading, IP throughput, Wi‑Fi integration or “one-box” capability need formal datasheets, option-code mapping, throughput profiles and test conditions, because the Anritsu comparison flags missing official datasheets, option-code cross-references and test conditions for several such claims [6].
The Keysight battle card similarly says “only platform,” “industry-leading,” “fully integrated,” “long-term scalability” and “lower TCO” are sales language and require formal datasheets, features documents, conformance reports or configuration tools before being treated as verifiable claims [61].
**No use of internal battle-card language as verified competitor fact unless independently supported.** Anritsu “fragmented tools” positioning can remain R&S sales positioning, but Anritsu’s own brochure supports that MX844030PC uses a common RTD GUI for protocol test case transfer, so the internal characterization cannot be treated as Anritsu official specification [9].
Internal O-RU competitor, price-point, market-share and test-coverage comparisons require official competitor datasheets, solution briefs, market reports, quotes, contracts or release notes before use as verified claims [14][18][21][43].
**Evidence for cost, TCO, support, warranty and calibration claims.** Sales statements such as fewer calibrations, fewer licenses, lower TCO and higher throughput are not supported by a TCO calculation in the cited battle card [8].
Competitor support or warranty claims require official service terms, since KeysightCare claims lack cited service-term documents and Anritsu support claims lack Anritsu official or third-party sources [13][63].
【推論】A defensible comparison package should therefore pair R&S CMX500/CMP180/CMP200 official specifications, feature documents, option codes, calibration conditions and conformance evidence with the competitor’s official datasheets/configuration/service/conformance evidence for the same test scope, and avoid “only,” “best,” “lower TCO,” “accepted,” or competitor-limitation claims unless those exact claims are supported by such evidence [10][25][35][49][50][61][63].
